DESIGN THESIS
Every encounter should be bespoke, native, legible, and worth remembering.
Quality target 10/10 does not mean difficulty target 10/10.
The player receives broad competitive tools; difficulty should come from interesting decisions, not grinding.
Hard is authored. Medium subtracts 2 opponent levels. Easy subtracts 4. Teams and AI remain identical.
Bosses may be near-lethal. Ordinary trainers must stay challenging without turning every route into a gauntlet.

DIFFICULTY PACING — PROVISIONAL AUDIT BANDS
ordinary_route: 7.5-8.4
notable_optional_or_route_ace: 8.5-9.0
mini_boss_or_faction_admin: 9.1-9.6
gym_leader_major_rival_faction_boss: 9.7-10.0
elite_four_champion_superboss: 10.0
These are advisory bands, not quotas. Judge each battle and the previous 8-10 encounters.

FATIGUE PRINCIPLE
A lower-pressure fight is not filler. It still needs a clean idea, legal set, real counterplay, and memorable identity.
Relief comes from fewer simultaneous demands, shorter teams, simpler information, or wider counterplay—not dumb AI.
Do not solve fatigue by making all later battles easier. Rebalance the whole campaign here before implementation.

CURRENT DIFFICULTY AUDIT — BATTLES 1-143
all_encounters: n=143, median=9.0, mean=8.95, range=7.5-10.0
ordinary_encounters: n=109, median=8.9, mean=8.88, range=7.7-9.6
recent_114_to_143: n=30, median=9.2, mean=9.22, range=8.7-10.0
ordinary_at_9.0_or_higher: 51 of 109
finding: Runtime proof is absent, but authored pressure is too concentrated near the ceiling to dismiss fatigue risk.
action: Re-audit the entire campaign here. Do not merely make future encounters easier and create a discontinuity.
action: Preserve clever teams and honest AI; create relief through team size, level offsets, simultaneous demands, and breadth of counterplay.

WORKFLOW

primary_question: How can the chosen starter beat its own same-generation counter without access to a captured team?

first_loss_lesson: Use the starter's legal utility, coverage, or a shop item to change the one-on-one instead of trading neutral attacks.

primary_question: Can the player identify the false ace, manage its support, and preserve an answer for the real Mew?
theme_and_tempo: Zorua leads beside Friend Guard Jigglypuff while Illusion makes it appear to be the Mew held in the final slot. Icy Wind and Helping Hand turn the false Mew into immediate pressure; Focus Sash Smeargle then creates a redirection or Fake Out window for the real Mew to use Nasty Plot and clean.
intentional_weakness: This team has several answers rather than one key. Spread attacks expose Illusion and bypass Follow Me, Taunt shuts down Jigglypuff or Smeargle, priority finishes a Sash-broken Smeargle, and early Bug, Ghost, and Dark options pressure Mew. The player can also double-target the support slot, contest speed with their own Icy Wind or Electroweb, or overwhelm the frail Zorua lead.
first_loss_lesson: Break Illusion early and remove the support slot before spending the team's best Dark, Bug, or Ghost answer.

difficulty_observed: UNPLAYED
fatigue_role: PENDING_AUDIT
primary_question: Can the player deny or route around Sticky Web before Rick's three physical attackers exploit it?
theme_and_tempo: Focus Sash Water Bubble Dewpider establishes Sticky Web while threatening real special coverage. Choice Band Anorith immediately punishes the Fire and Flying attacks invited by the Bug theme, Eviolite No Guard Karrablast is the only setup threat, and level-16 Life Orb Larvesta closes through recoil-limited physical pressure and U-turn rather than a mature Quiver Dance sweep.
intentional_weakness: Taunt, multihit attacks, or immediate pressure can deny Web; Flying and Levitate Pokémon ignore it, and legal removal clears it. Wingull, Shinx, Blitzle, Rotom, Bonsly, Rock coverage, priority, and faster Choice users are already available. Intimidate, burns, and physical walls constrain the three backliners, while Water and Rock pressure force Larvesta to spend recoil or recovery turns. No one counter is required.
first_loss_lesson: Stop Web, clear it, or bring Flying and Levitate pieces rather than allowing every later exchange to occur at reduced Speed.

theme_and_tempo: Light Ball Lightning Rod Pikachu and Toxic Orb Guts Taillow lead with Fake Out, Electroweb speed control, priority, immediate damage, and protection from Electric targeting. Eviolite Dry Skin Paras and Sitrus Quick Feet Zigzagoon form the back-line setup mode: Rage Powder or Spore can buy Belly Drum, then Extreme Speed supplies pressure.
intentional_weakness: The opening pair is vulnerable to Ground, Rock, Intimidate, and coordinated targeting; Protect can also expose Fake Out or consume Taillow's first Guts turn. Dreepy, Rotom, and other Ghosts ignore Extreme Speed and Facade, while Intimidate and burns hinder Zigzagoon. The player can disrupt either wave without predicting a forced opening.
first_loss_lesson: Preserve disruption or a Ghost for the second wave instead of spending every answer on the fast lead pair.
